messages:
ravi: FYI noticed a pattern: clients hitting 204 then immediate reconnects, but only for requests routed through the new low-latency pool. reconnect-rate spike ~11:03 UTC.

anya: same. looks like the pool's resume_ttl config was set low in the canary (50ms). that makes a 204 mean tombstoned. clients (many older SDKs) re-open instantly.

ben: logs: [11:03:10] proxy: route=chat-stream status=204 resume_ttl=50ms conn=322 closed_upstream
[11:03:10] client-sdk: reconnect attempt=1 backoff=0s
[11:03:11] billing: session.create token=tok_55 id=evt_7

ravi: infra-bot: show session.create delta + top tokens?

infra-bot: [automated] session.create rate for route "chat-stream" increased 2.7x between 11:02 and 11:06 UTC. top repeated tokens: tok_55, tok_11, tok_77.

anya: mitigation: revert resume_ttl change (rolling back now). longer-term: server-side soft-204 debounce (200-400ms) + billing idempotency header. also console: add per-route reconnect spike alert and overlay flag-change widget.

ben: small nuance: low resume_ttl was intended for faster failover; we should instead make router prefer sticky rejoin if reconnect happens within X ms to avoid cross-pool pain.

ravi: agree. owners: server debounce (anya), router sticky rejoin probe (ben), billing dedupe (niranjan), console overlay + alert (josh). devex: add blurb recommending exponential backoff for 204 and jumpy pools.

devex: will add quickstart note and sample backoff snippet (100-500ms jitter) and link incident.

console-bot: [automated] Created ticket CON-6210: reconnect spike overlay + recent-flag-toggles heatmap.

ravi: rollback complete at 11:09 UTC, metrics trending down. Ill kick off a 30m post-incident to capture rollout guardrails. Closing thread once tickets assigned. :white_check_mark:
